* Scan the 5 × 6 board for every legal capture (my piece adjacent orthogonally to an opponent piece).  
* For each capture candidate, simulate the capture on a temporary copy of the board.  
* After the capture evaluate how many capture opportunities I will have on my **next** turn – i.e. count how many of my pieces are orthogonally next to at least one opponent piece.  
* Choose the move that maximises that number.  This encourages me to keep the board “dense” and avoid isolating my pieces, which tends to give more future moves and, in practice, a higher chance of winning the game.  
* If several moves have the same maximal value, we break ties deterministically by preferring the move that appears first in a fixed row‑major scan (up, right, down, left) – guaranteeing reproducible behaviour.

Because the board is tiny, this evaluation is fast enough (well under 1 ms) and it yields a strong baseline policy that beats many naïve bots.
